days.label: Zion history and a relaxed south-entrance day

stops.name: Zion Canyon Visitor Center
stops.note: Spend a little time with the outdoor exhibits and ask about access beyond the closed canyon road. If parking is full, use designated parking in Springdale and check the shuttle arrangements.
stops.why: A short orientation leaves the rest of the day open for actual visits rather than transport guesswork.

stops.name: Zion Nature Center
stops.note: Spend time at the Nature Center; check its opening hours and access before setting out.
stops.why: This gives you a second named place to explore without relying on the closed canyon road.

stops.name: Human History Museum
stops.note: Explore the exhibits and orientation film, then take in the outdoor views of the Towers of the Virgin and Bridge Mountain. Check museum hours before you go.
stops.why: The exhibits and views make a substantial afternoon experience at a relaxed pace.

days.label: An after-rain afternoon at the museum patio and Canyon Overlook

stops.name: Zion Human History Museum Patio
stops.note: After noon, take an unhurried photography break here if the patio is accessible and conditions allow.
stops.why: Starting later keeps the rainy morning free while leaving room for a relaxed photo outing.

stops.name: Canyon Overlook
stops.note: Check Zion–Mt. Carmel Highway and overlook access before traveling; don't use the closed canyon road. Go only if conditions are safe after the rain, and skip the overlook if the route or footing is wet or slippery.
stops.why: This keeps the canyon viewpoint as an optional finish rather than heading to exposed terrain during the rainy morning.

alternatives.name: Human History Museum
alternatives.note: If rain persists or the overlook is unsafe or inaccessible, revisit the indoor exhibits if the museum is open; check its hours first.

stops.name: Kolob Canyons Visitor Center
stops.note: Stop for the exhibits and ask a ranger about current access in Kolob Canyons. The NPS listing says the center closes daily from noon to 1 p.m.; check its hours for your dates.
stops.why: This is a useful starting point for a part of Zion you haven’t explored on the canyon days.

stops.name: Kolob Canyons
stops.note: Spend the rest of your visit taking in the landscape at an unhurried pace, choosing where to linger once you know what is accessible that day.
stops.why: Giving Kolob its own day avoids squeezing a separate area into an already full Zion Canyon outing.

narrativeSections.markdown: Kolob Canyons is a separate outing: the NPS places its visitor center 45 miles north of Springdale. Keeping it on day three leaves the first two days focused on Zion Canyon and preserves the relaxed pace. Check access and transportation arrangements for the canyon stops before settling on the exact order of each day.
